#109255. Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

Diablo 4's next season is short, but it lets you become The Butcher, and it has Doom: The Dark Ages skins you probably can't afford

📅 06 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (858 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The massive Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods.
  • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
  • Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The massive Diablo 4 Developer Update has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

Patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the new Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a newly introduced event that rewards you for killing enemies quickly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

It has been revealed that elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a new activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

It has been revealed that the Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

According to recent reports, anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

In a recent development, there are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a upcoming item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

Recent findings suggest that even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the fresh season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

It has been revealed that the trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the fresh class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

Industry observers note that the more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

While soulslikes went bigger than substantial, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the substantial, bulging ones.
  • Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition.
  • According to recent reports, still, it’s clever with its limitations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the substantial, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

According to recent reports, still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

In a recent development, which is welcome, as these big lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

According to recent reports, recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

According to recent reports, I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

Will GTA 6 break the internet? UK broadband operator braces for impact, saying "GTA 6 has been on our radar for a long time"

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that as Grand Theft Auto 6 breaks pre-order records on the PlayStation and Xbox stores, and looks poised to break many more sales records once it launches next week, questions of whether it will also break the internet arise.
  • It has been revealed that major game releases register nationally for broadband use: we know this from an investigation into gaming downloads and how much they cost the environment we published in 2021.
  • For this reason, Openreach - the manufacturer that runs the largest broadband network in the UK - has been tracking Rockstar's latest game closely.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as Grand Theft Auto 6 breaks pre-order records on the PlayStation and Xbox stores, and looks poised to break many more sales records once it launches next week, questions of whether it will also break the internet arise. Collective network load will undoubtedly spike around its release - will regional infrastructure be able to bear it?

It has been revealed that major game releases register nationally for broadband use: we know this from an investigation into gaming downloads and how much they cost the environment we published in 2021. We also know that UK communications regulator Ofcom negotiates with gaming companies to try and avoid major game launches happening alongside major cultural occasions, such as sporting events, which are likely to spike broadband use. The network pipes can be clogged, and there's arguably never been a game as anticipated as GTA 6 to clog them.

For this reason, Openreach - the manufacturer that runs the largest broadband network in the UK - has been tracking Rockstar's latest game closely. "GTA 6 has been on our radar for a long time," Trevor Linney, Openreach's director for network technology, told Eurogamer. "We know from games like Fortnite and Call of Duty that a major release or update can drive huge amounts of data across the network, so it'll be fascinating to see just how much GTA moves the needle. Our network and teams are ready, and GTA 6 is certainly one we'll be watching for a upcoming download record.".

In a recent development, A spokesperson for Ofcom, meanwhile, noted: "Broadband networks should be well placed to handle this download. Ofcom's Broadband Code of Practice means providers must give customers clear, realistic information and guarantee a minimum speed. If you’re not getting this, you may be able to leave your contract penalty-free. Check your speed now, so you can focus on the game rather than the loading screen." Ofcom has a website with sections devoted to broadband speeds and changing providers, in case you're interested.

According to recent reports, alongside yesterday's announcements that GTA 6 had become the most pre-ordered game in Xbox Store and PlayStation Store history, Sony and Microsoft shared strongly worded advice that players download the game ahead of time to avoid complications caused by "unprecedented demand". We saw last year what happened when Hollow Knight: Silksong arrived, causing chaos on Xbox, Steam, and Nintendo servers, and that game's reach was an order of magnitude less than GTA 6's. I don't recall a Selfridges store takeover in London for Silksong - do you?

The wait for GTA 6 is finally nearly over, as it arrives next Thursday, 19th November.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Patch, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.
  • The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.
  • In a recent development, since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Patch, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

In a recent development, since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

Industry observers note that the Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

It has been revealed that the Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

Recent findings suggest that the Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

Recent findings suggest that the Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside fresh Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

In a recent development, lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the substantial day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three big updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each enhancement may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

Recent findings suggest that coming up in mid-December, there's the Junker starting scenario, which I assume is all about trading scrap, rather than being a Prussian nobleman. You'll get a bespoke perk, fresh items, and the ability to hire, equip and send scavs on expeditions. This patch will also include some minor expansions for the Fence and Gunsmith vocations – the latter will be able to flog or otherwise make use of shotgun shells, 25mm grenade rounds and a tier 3 handmade SMG, alongside new armour.

Late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major update. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

Recent findings suggest that last but not least, the planned April update will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

In a recent development, are you playing Probably Stolen? It's been doing better than expected. I was keen on the demo, but my attention was lured away by a truly upsetting game about dogpeople in caves.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox boss Asha Sharma has confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in development at MachineGames, the Swedish studio behind the acclaimed Wolfenstein: The New Order, Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossal, and 2024's celebrated Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. Additionally, she revealed Doom developer idSoftware - one of the Microsoft-owned studios heavily impacted by sweeping Xbox job cuts earlier this year - is now working on a new game.

According to recent reports, sharma has, of course, been on a bit of a PR offensive of late, positioning herself alongside snippets of positive news at a time Xbox is embroiled in a massive business "reset" effort that has resulted in proposed studio closures and mass layoffs that will ultimately see 3,200 Xbox employees lose their jobs. This week's Wolfenstein 3 reveal similarly arrived in the form of a tweet posted directly from her social media account.

"Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at MachineGames," Sharma wrote on X. "One of gaming's most crucial franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more." As for idSoftware's fresh project, confirmation of that - again attributed directly to Sharma - appeared in a post on Bethesda's website. "Slaughter Mode comes to Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations on Monday," she wrote, "and the team is already working on its next game.".

Sources indicate that in July, sweeping job cuts at Xbox resulted in 96 of idSoftware's 136 employees being laid off in a move one former team member described as a "bloodbath". Since then, idSoftware co-studio director Marty Stratton has attempted to downplay the cuts, recently insisting the studio was "doing great". He added id was "working more closely than ever" with MachineGames - a studio which appears to have escaped Sharma's restructuring efforts so far.

This week's Wolfenstein and idSoftware news follows similar efforts by Xbox to reassure fans their favourite franchises are unaffected by the recent layoffs. Shortly after substantial job cuts at Bethesda were confirmed, the company moved to insist The Elder Scrolls 6 was still "on the way" and that its prepares were "unaffected" (the company has since released a trailer announcing its subtitle). It also confirmed a new Fallout game was in development.

Xbox's year of bad news - which includes ongoing boycott efforts relating to Microsoft's controversial involvement with the Israeli military - comes as the division celebrates its 25th anniversary. Earlier this week, Sharma shared a memo to staff marking the occasion, albeit one in which she seemingly championed a gen-AI future for games development, enthusing that, "A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

Industry observers note that the open test was largely well-received, and players actually demonstrated up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Recent findings suggest that numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that slay the Spire 2, which released into early access earlier this year, is expanding once more with a major new beta update. This introduces the deckbuilder's first new character since launch - a whimsical musician armed with a bow - alongside two new modes, and more.

In a recent development, when Slay the Spire 2 arrived back in March, it was to much enthusiastic acclaim. Eurogamer's Bertie Purchie is a major fan, and has trumpeted its successes on multiple occasions, calling the sequel's co-op mode "transformative". And it was a commercial hit too, managing to shift over 5m copies in just a month of release. All of which means there are plenty of eyes on Slay the Spire 2, eager to see what developer MegaCrit does next.

It has been revealed that so far major updates have brought the likes of buffs, balance adjustments, art updates, UI improvements, bug fixes, and more - and MegaCrit has also made other substantial adjustments including the jettisoning of third act boss Doormaker, after it decided the encounter was overly complex. And now, as 2026 nears its conclusion, the studio has released its "biggest (beta) patch yet", including a sweep of major additions.

In a recent development, as per MegaCrit's v0.113.0 patch notes, the headliner is The Fool; Slay the Spire 2's first latest character, who's described as a "silly musician who wields a bow". Unsurprisingly, The Fool doesn't arrive in their final form, and the studio claims it expects to make a "great number of content and balance changes" before the character is ready for the main branch.

Accompanying The Fool are two new game modes: Blitz and Dread. Blitz is described as a "condensed and chaotic" mode focused on deckbuilding. Unlocked after completing an Ascension run of any difficulty, it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across all characters. "The Merchant's wares feel a bit off," MegaCrit teases, "the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters??".

It has been revealed that if you're looking for a more gruelling challenge, though, there's the "brutally difficult" new Dread mode, designed for players who've reached Ascension 10 on all characters, including The Fool. All ascension modifiers are enabled, according to MegaCrit, while bosses are stronger and buff all enemies found across their Act. And if that's still not enough to get your heart racing, MegaCrit notes curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire.

According to recent reports, beyond the headline stuff, v0.113.0 tweaks rest sites so they appear one floor earlier every act, and that's alongside the usual list of UI changes, art additions, nerfs, balance adjustments, and more. Full patch notes can be found on Steam.

Industry observers note that those players eager to put Slay the Spire 2's latest additions through their paces will need to enable the beta branch by right-clicking on Slay the Spire 2 in their Steam library and navigating to Properties > Game Versions & Betas and selecting 'public-beta' from the dropdown menu. MegaCrit notes the game's main branch has also been updated with all content and changes from the previous beta.

According to recent reports, with less than a week to go before GTA 6's hugely anticipated release, the game's final map - or at least a stylised poster version of it, depicting the state of Leonida's key landmarks - has surfaced online. It was reportedly snapped during Selfridge's sizable GTA 6's takeover, and is seemingly the physical map included in Rockstar's £350 collector's edition.

Fans have been pondering GTA 6's map for some time now, cross-referencing previous map leaks with official trailer footage in an attempt to gain some insight into the major landmarks and regions Rockstar has in store. And while the newly leaked map is far from granular, it does at least appear to confirm Leonida's rough layout and the key locations players can visit this time.

Assuming the map's veracity, it's all rendered in an art style somewhere between mid-century tourism poster and Adult Swim, featuring the phrase "The Goodtime State" up top - a riff on the actual Florida's nickname, The Sunshine State - while Leonida's most notable points of interest are interspersed with cartoon figures.

In a recent development, there's a toking turtle (or possibly a tortoise - I'm no expert), a golfer proudly wearing assless chaps, a flying saucer, and more. I'll spare you the geographic details confirmed on the map in case you want to go in unspoiled. One point of amusement though: the way the map photo is cropped means fans searching for confirmation of an in-game Key West are still none the wiser.

Sources indicate that it's not entirely clear where the wonkily angled photo originated from, but prominent Rockstar Games community insider Videotech, who shared the image on social media, suggested it came from a "naughty Selfridges employee" during Selfridges' GTA 6 takeover. The map itself appears to be the "double-Sided souvenir poster with map of Leonida" included in Rockstar's eyewateringly expensive GTA 6 Collector's Edition. This costs £350 and doesn't come with a copy of the game. Or assless chaps, for that matter.

It has been revealed that this isn't the first time GTA 6's map - officially mentioned to be twice the size of GTA 5's - has leaked online, although previous leaks have been notably more controversial. Earlier this year, a group calling itself CyberLeek shared unofficial gameplay and map details in the name of what it called "Gamers' Rights". In August, with Netflix's official GTA 6 unveiling looming, the group cashed out nearly £200,000 from its crypto scheme.

Amid all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion has been delayed until next week, meaning a verdict could arrive just as GTA 6 goes on sale.

Avoiding Steam Machine this Black Friday? Here's what other mini PCs can actually get you for your cash

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Steam Machine is now "checkout-ready" according to Valve, but with a $1,049 starting price for the 512GB base model (and that $1,349 rate on the 2TB version up for debate in the near-future), there's a problem for those who don't want to break four figures on a newly introduced system.
  • That's where the well-established (but recently far more popular) world of mini PCs comes in.
  • These devices have been finding themselves in more homes this year, as increased prices of the best gaming PCs and even cheaper components have pushed both those after a productivity and gaming solution towards more budget-friendly alternatives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Steam Machine is now "checkout-ready" according to Valve, but with a $1,049 starting price for the 512GB base model (and that $1,349 rate on the 2TB version up for debate in the near-future), there's a problem for those who don't want to break four figures on a newly introduced system.

That's where the well-established (but recently far more popular) world of mini PCs comes in. Whether you want more options further down the price range or you're after something with more graphical grunt, these compact PCs prove it's not just Valve producing ready-to-go gaming machines that don't take up floor space.

These devices have been finding themselves in more homes this year, as increased prices of the best gaming PCs and even cheaper components have pushed both those after a productivity and gaming solution towards more budget-friendly alternatives.

I've spent the last few months road-testing mini PCs from Geekom to Asus, spanning the full price range. Right at the bottom, boxes like the $499 Geekom A5 2027 Edition will gear themselves heavily towards indie titles and retro emulation. At the top, you'll find full dedicated GPU options spanning up to the RTX 5070.

It's worth noting that the Windows operating system won't give you that living-room-console ease of the Steam Machine, but instead opens you up to more versatility around launchers and OS compatibility.

Like you, I was curious to see what these tiny little rigs could actually conjure - and you'll find out exactly how each price point fared in my benchmarks just below.

Sources indicate that I've spent the last six months running my everyday workflow through mini PCs across a range of brands, testing every compact rig I can get my hands on in whatever games they allow for. Around that, I've also been testing and reviewing gaming laptops on GamesRadar+ for the last six years, using similar components in different configurations every two weeks.

In a recent development, the best deal you'll find on the budget Geekom A5 2027 Edition right now sits with Amazon. A $50 discount on the original $549 takes us to $499 this Black Friday. While prices have been jumping since the start of the year here, that's cheaper than it has been since July. This one's dropped to around $400 earlier in 2026, though.

In a recent development, the Geekom A5 2027 Edition is a productivity machine first and foremost. The AMD Ryzen 7 7730U under the hood is designed to run efficiently, quietly, and with minimal power draw. That means it can hum away in the background without breaking the bank, but it also sweeps away a lot of the power more demanding games require.

In a recent development, I was still curious to see how gaming actually fares at the lower end of the budget. In short, this thing will run your indie Steam library no problem. If you prioritize smaller titles, you'll get on just fine here and likely kick yourself if you opt for anything more expensive. Retro emulation runs nicely as well, if that's your jam.

That's about as far as you'll get, though. Shadow of the Tomb Raider, an older "double-A" release that doesn't tend to make too many gaming laptops sweat, neared smooth framerates only with resolution set to 720p and settings dropped to their lowest. Medium can just about squeak by on a smaller screen at 28fps.

The same story is true of Cyberpunk 2077, the substantial guns test. Without frame generation you're looking at 27fps at 720p here, though we do jump up nicely to 45fps with a little extra help.

According to recent reports, these more demanding games are playable. They run. You can even get over 30fps if you make larger sacrifices - a perfectly decent position at the budget end of the spectrum. They're just not going to feel nearly as good as they might slightly further up the price scale.

The GMKTec K8 Plus has dropped under $700 in the past, but today's $170 discount is a starting point. I'd keep a close eye on this one as Black Friday progresses, rather than diving in straight away now - this one stands to wriggle under that $700 threshold if we're lucky.

Recent findings suggest that the GMKTec K8 Plus upgrades your processor to the Ryzen 7 8845HS, adds an Oculink connection for future eGPU upgrades, and includes extra support for more monitor displays. That's a set of upgrades that will set you up for more demanding games a lot better than the budget-minded Geekom A5.

In practice, that means solid 40+fps in Shadow of the Tomb Raider at both medium and high settings in 1080p, with Cyberpunk 2077 managing 41fps in medium as well. You've got a lot more breathing room here, as well as power ceiling that allows for that FHD resolution.

Mid-range "double-As" are more-than possible with a few tweaks, and more demanding titles are within reach here as well.

In a recent development, ultimately, this is your all-rounder. It's powerful enough to represent solid value for money across chunkier games while still giving you room to grow with that eGPU connection and easily upgradeable innards.

I have one major caveat from my testing, though. You might need to upgrade the Wi-Fi card when you buy it. Internet was incredibly slow for me during testing, far slower than any other device on my network. There's something funky going on behind the scenes here, but users have reported a fresh card solves the problem.

In a recent development, the Geekom A9 Max is available with that Ryzen Ai 9 HX470 chipset, 2TB SSD and 32GB RAM for $1,499. Again this one has been cheaper this year so far, so it's worth watching over the next week. Still, it's been locked in at $1600 since August.

The Geekom A9 Max is a step up in price compared to our more budget-friendly alternatives, and overtakes the 2TB Steam Machine cost. So what's in it for you?

According to recent reports, this is actually a very similar value proposition to the Steam Machine, hitting 30+fps in Cyberpunk 2077 at 1440p Medium settings without any frame generation help. Adding frame-gen into the equation, and it's easy to speed well past that 60fps threshold. It's a step up where more demanding games like CD Projekt Red's open world are concerned, though improvements further down the scale are more measured compared to the GMKTec further up.

In a recent development, what's going to separate these two rigs, though, is what else you want to do with your PC. The Geekom A9 Max can match the Steam Machine in overall performance, but it also adds a whole workstation into your purchase.

Industry observers note that this is where Windows plays its most important card in this trip into mini PC land. While you won't have that console-like operating system, you'll have everything you need for demanding productivity tasks and workflows on top of that gaming performance. It's the better option for those not just buying a gaming device, but rolling their purchase in with their work machine.

It has been revealed that we're down to a brand-new record-low price on the RTX 5070 Asus ROG GR70 mini PC this Black Friday, with the $2,599 configuration shedding $300 from the final price. This one's only ever dipped just below $2,500 in previous sales, though it's still one of the most expensive mini PCs on the market.

The largest, and most expensive, mini PC I've had on my test bench so far, the Asus ROG GR70 isn't a budget alternative to the Steam Machine but an additional investment in more demanding PC games. This is a full system, with a dedicated RTX 5070 graphics card humming away inside, and some of AMD's most powerful processors up top as well.

It has been revealed that I tested the AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX3D / RTX 5070 version with a whopping 64GB RAM under the hood. That's a particularly expensive configuration in today's rates, one that comes in at around $2,800.

For that kind of cash, you can easily pick up one of the best gaming laptops or a cheaper full-tower PC - so the ROG GR70 is only for those specifically seeking a miniature form factor.

How did it go? Unsurprisingly, for a rig often twice the price of the Steam Machine, pretty damn smoothly. Triple-figure frame rates are the norm for most Triple-As in high settings at FHD, while we're still well above 60fps in everything at 1440p as well.

That's performance that's going to blow the Steam Machine out the water, but it's still tracking behind other RTX 5070 counterparts. The value of this beast compared to an RTX 5070 gaming laptop or desktop PC doesn't quite stack up - you'll need to know you're in it for the miniature footprint for this premium pick to make sense.

We're also rounding up the best gaming handhelds and best gaming tablets for more ways to play this holiday season.

Managing Editor of Hardware at GamesRadar+, I originally landed in hardware at our sister site TechRadar before moving over to GamesRadar. In between, I've written for Tom’s Guide, Wireframe, The Indie Game Website and That Video Game Blog, covering everything from the PS5 launch to the Apple Pencil. Now, i'm focused on Nintendo Switch, gaming laptops (and the keyboards, headsets and mice that come with them), PS5, and trying to find the perfect projector.

Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

📅 10 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (517 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3.
  • In a recent development, today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB.
  • To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related problems.

In a recent development, today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja noted it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

It has been revealed that in the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

Industry observers note that you can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

Sources indicate that there’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

A new report reckons 40% of developers in the video games industry are using generative AI - but even more think it's harmful

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (517 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a newly introduced report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work.
  • That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.
  • Recent findings suggest that the report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a newly introduced report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work. This is up four percent compared to the same report last year.

That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.

Recent findings suggest that the report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations". There appears to be a significant split between triple-A studios that use gen-AI (with 27 percent of triple-A developers noting that they "feel encouraged or pressured" to use it) and indie devs, of which only nine percent say the same. Perhaps unsurprisingly - given how vocally against gen-AI a lot of 'frontline developers' have been - the tools are mostly used by "business operations and services, mobile-only studios, and free-to-play developers".

There seems to be a gap in the ages of those willing to use AI tools as well; per the report, over half (54 percent) of people 45 years or older reported using the tools - an eight-point increase from last year's survey. There is also more usage among men (45 percent) than women (33 percent).

What is perhaps more striking is that more people responded to the survey saying that they think AI is having a negative impact on games (55 percent) than responded saying they use the tech, suggesting a trend of caution rather than widespread adoption. Notably, respondents saying they are wary of the technology increased one percent since last year, so more people think AI is having a negative effect on the industry now than at the same time in 2025. Perhaps that's because of the sweeping layoffs we've seen across the games industry, often mentioned in the same breath as AI. Or the 'AI slop' that's been flooding Steam and pushing more traditional developers out. Orr some of the abysmal projects we've seen launch that have clearly used gen-AI assets.

"I did not get into a creative industry to hand over the creativity to an algorithm," remarked one respondent from the UK when explaining why they don't use gen-AI tools. "I got into this industry to collaborate with creative people, not to have an advanced chatbot riff on the ideas of someone who was laid off," said another from California. "I believe that no one should have to read what no human has written and shouldn't have to see what no human has created," said yet another from Minnesota.

The use of generative AI remains controversial in the games industry, though with substantial companies like Epic and Microsoft doubling down on the tech, it seems this split between developers that want to embrace it and those that don't is only growing larger.

Toby Fox, the creator of Deltarune (and Undertale), has this week released his 'Fall 2026' newsletter, giving fans a "status update" on Chapter 6...and Chapter 7.

Firstly, Chapter 6 is "progressing well", and the game is now a "structurally complete draft" that can be played from start to finish. In saying this, it will still take a "bit longer" to finish up some other scenes and details:.

"Much of the game looks complete… but, some key scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing.

It has been revealed that "Even though Chapter 6 is a rather short chapter, I would like it to be as good as possible. I won't be able to rush this.".

According to recent reports, as for the recent vote, Queen is officially the winner, taking out 65% of the votes. And the reward is a "stupid scene" from Chapter 6.

Industry observers note that and if this wasn't already enough, there's the Chapter 7 development enhancement. The team has "only just started", and Fox has read out some of the events and dialogue to the team, but is withholding the rest of the story until they "complete more of the game".

According to recent reports, I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens.

Everyone agrees it's more fun this way.

Team members who completed their work on Chapter 6 have moved onto Chapter 7 now. Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!

It has been revealed that fox ends the latest update, reminding fans how the team has expanded since Chapter 4, but "more and more time is necessary" to keep the game's development going at the "fastest pace possible". 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Sims 4 will soon get a latest patch to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Sources indicate that going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis remarked this will work with fresh and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in latest saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

In a recent development, you may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a newly introduced lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an enhancement that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

It has been revealed that catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that to get into the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe in GTA 6, you can either obtain the safe code, which is far harder than it sounds, or you can blow it open, which is the much easier way to get in. If you'd still rather unlock the safe the classic way, I'll explain both methods of getting into the safe below, including how to get the GTA 6 bowling alley safe code. Whichever road you go down, it'll help you save up some cash and get back on your feet - and take down a few of those pesky Kolt gang members while you're at it.

Sources indicate that the GTA 6 Bowling Alley safe code is 0300. To find it for yourself, you need to go to Brooks Boatworks, as hinted at in the notepad next to the safe. The safe code is on a map on the wall in one of the buildings there, as marked on the image above.

By the time the bowling alley is mentioned, Brooks Boatworks should be marked on your map as another location held by the Kolt crew, and you may have even raided it already. Whether you've been there or not, the map is found on the wall of an office in the raised buildings to the east of the area, and you can find two other GTA 6 safe codes on this map, too.

Recent findings suggest that you'll have to fend off a lot of Kolt members at both the bowling alley and the boatworks, so make sure you've got some decent GTA 6 guns to hand, and certainly as much Zombix as you can carry. You'll find more at each location, too, so keep an eye out.

You'll also see the option to plant explosives on the GTA 6 bowling alley safe, but if you haven't got the right explosives to hand, the option is grayed out. Fortunately, there are some sticky bombs conveniently stashed in the next room, meaning it's the much safer option that heading out to the boatworks.

Recent findings suggest that we previously believed this option required reaching one of the Chapter 3 GTA 6 missions, at which point you unlock the ability to buy sticky bombs from Ammu-Nation, but with the few explosives available in the bowling alley, you're golden. Keep the spares on you, and you can use them to get into other safes around Leonida, too.

#109229. Marvel Cosmic Invasion’s Castle Doom Feels More Spinoff Than DLC

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1303 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thegamer ↗ Open Full Page

Marvel Cosmic Invasion’s Castle Doom Feels More Spinoff Than DLC

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1303 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, adding a roguelike or roguelite mode to a game post-launch to keep people playing has become a popular and pretty effective trend.
  • Although I really should have had faith in Tribute Games to do right by roguelite expansions after what they did with Shredder's Revenge.
  • I’m pleased to report that my skepticism was misplaced.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, adding a roguelike or roguelite mode to a game post-launch to keep people playing has become a popular and pretty effective trend. The Last of Us Part 2 and God of War Ragnarok are just two examples of games that have been praised for their roguelike DLC, but despite the trend’s success and my love for almost all things roguelike, I was skeptical of whether it was the right move for Marvel’s Cosmic Invasion.

Although I really should have had faith in Tribute Games to do right by roguelite expansions after what they did with Shredder's Revenge.

I’m pleased to report that my skepticism was misplaced. Not only does it turn out that the building blocks set in place by Cosmic Invasion’s base game were the perfect foundation on which to build an unexpectedly entertaining roguelite mode, but the upcoming blocks placed on top of them have made its Siege of Castle Doom expansion feel more like a spinoff than a DLC.

I liked Cosmic Invasion a lot. So much so that ever since I returned to lay siege to Castle Doom, I’ve been racking my brains trying to figure out why I fell off before I made it to the end of the base game. I love everything Marvel (maybe a little too much), and started playing video games in the ‘90s, so naturally a 2D beat ‘em up designed to look like it could have been released during that golden era for the genre ticks just about all my boxes.

It’s also the best this revived genre has had to offer in an era where we have been spoiled by classic beat ‘em ups tied to IP.

Recent findings suggest that there’s no risk of me falling off the Cosmic Invasion bandwagon again, at least not until Doctor Doom is dealt with, both in the game and on the substantial screen. The Castle Doom DLC adds what is effectively a roguelite mode. Choose your heroes and lay siege to the castle, progressing up through its various levels, the enemies you face getting more powerful, and the man himself, the formidable Doctor Doom, waiting for you at the end.

According to recent reports, like a roguelite, you progress by clearing rooms or areas so that you can move onto the next one. You’re presented with options as you move between rooms; the symbols on the door representing what you’ll get or face in the next, very similar to the decisions you’re presented with when moving between rooms in Hades.

In a recent development, the green symbol, for example, means you’ll enter a room where you can refill your health. The blue symbol, however, will present you with more battery charges. These are key, as you need to charge your batteries to make it deeper into the castle. You have to do this before Doom’s gauge - the green one in the opposite corner of the screen - is full. Enemies get faster and more aggressive as it fills, and once it’s full, your run ends.

Once a run ends, some of those battery charges come with you. They can then be exchanged in Reed’s Lab to unlock items and events for your subsequent runs, potentially making them less challenging. Again, leaning into those roguelite elements. You can also select temporary buffs that expire at the end of each run after every three full charges, having to choose between improvements that will help you attack, defend, or boost your tactical prowess.

Recent findings suggest that I’m really only scratching the surface of what you can do in this newly introduced mode, which is why, again, it feels more like its own game than an extension of Cosmic Invasion. I’ve not even touched on the two new characters it adds to the roster yet either - Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom.

Yes, you can be Doom to fight Doom, and he might be the best character in the game.

The two fresh additions continue a trend of something so difficult to nail in the beat ‘em up genre, and that’s making sure every character feels unique. Cosmic Invasion’s roster is already bigger than most beat ‘em ups’, so another two characters feeling this different again is quite the feat.

Doom is, naturally, all about feeling powerful. Not only is his moveset easy to learn and master, but everything he does feels big and impactful. So much so that using him is almost like lowering the difficulty. I mean, he’s battling through a castle built by his variant, so that kind of makes sense.

Invisible Woman is the exact opposite. Her move set is so different from anyone else in Cosmic Invasion that it took a few runs for me to really get a feel for how she works. She shields herself rather than blocks or evades, just like in the comics and the movies, and to really get the most out of her, you need to be attuned to what she can do and what she’s capable of. That includes turning invisible and phasing through enemies when you sprint, and throwing up what is effectively a shield that also deals damage when you hold square (or the relevant button on your platform of choice).

In a recent development, even when using characters who have been in the game since launch, it feels entirely different. No, the DLC technically hasn’t altered them in any way, but the upcoming mode poses a new challenge. You’re not just fighting to the end of a level anymore. This is an onslaught that’s going to take time and tenacity. You need to be more methodical in your approach. You can’t just wade in with Wolverine and take damage while you slash away. Do that, and you’ll be done before your first full charge.

Cosmic Invasion getting Doom DLC two months before Avengers: Doomsday is, of course, no accident. We are, unfortunately, well beyond the era of movies being able to have tie-in games that release simultaneously. Instead, studios have to come up with more inventive ways to create brand synergy, and this is a fantastic way to do it.

As I may have already mentioned, I’m a huge Marvel fan. Doomsday is the most excited I’ve been about a movie since Avengers: Endgame, and anything that gives me more Doom between now and then is incredibly welcome. It helps that it’s as well done as the Castle Doom DLC, and it will be an expansion I keep playing after Doomsday has rolled through and the terrifying latest MCU villain has torn through all of the heroes I’ve formed emotional attachments to over the last two decades, thoroughly ruining my Christmas.

He’s going to kill everyone, isn’t he?

Recent findings suggest that as much as I like Cosmic Invasion, it never struck me as a game that would have a long shelf life, because beat ‘em ups rarely do. Tribute Games has gone above and beyond to keep the game in the zeitgeist and put it back on the radar in a major way just in time for what may well end up being the biggest theatrical release ever.

If you fell off of Cosmic Invasion for whatever reason, like me, or you finished the game, you now have the perfect reason to go back. The Siege of Castle Doom forces you to reinvent your approach, feels like an entirely fresh experience without detracting from the fantastic game Cosmic Invasion already was, and best of all, it only costs $7.99. Even if you defy the odds and take Doom out on your first run, it’s worth $8 for the euphoric feeling you’ll have if you somehow manage to pull off such a feat.

You definitely will not pull off such a feat.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game.
  • The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.
  • Sources indicate that on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

Sources indicate that on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

Recent findings suggest that with the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

Sources indicate that that same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

Recent findings suggest that it’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

  • In any case, the revision goes a tad further than that.

A major part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 upgrade next week that adds in a newly introduced game plus mode.

According to recent reports, "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

In any case, the revision goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

Overall, a bit of a smaller upgrade compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something key or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

Crimson Desert studio is implementing AI "throughout our entire development pipeline," and expects DokeV to launch in 2028

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow.
  • The South Korean studio mentioned as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed.".
  • "However, AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity, while the core gameplay experience and actual content creation remain fully driven by our development team," the developer noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow.

The South Korean studio mentioned as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed.".

"However, AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity, while the core gameplay experience and actual content creation remain fully driven by our development team," the developer noted.

Sources indicate that when Crimson Desert first launched, players spotted a crop of suspicious in-game images that looked like they were prompted into existence. Pearl Abyss soon explained that some "2D visual props" were generated with AI tools, but were always intended to be replaced with human-made art, before quickly patching them out of the hit open-world game.

According to recent reports, it seems Pearl Abyss is now even more keen on the controversial tech, however: "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality. AI is being utilized across various stages of development - including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization - and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline. We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality. We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously.".

In a recent development, elsewhere in the letter, the studio mentioned its previously declared creature-collector DokeV is "targeting a launch in the second half of 2028" and we should hear more about it within the year. DokeV was initially targeting a 2023 launch a few years ago. Meanwhile, Crimson Desert is being prepped for a Nintendo Switch 2 launch "in the first half of next year.".

The use of generative AI in game development has been a hot topic for years, though it's only become more prevalent in recent months as 'AI slop' floods Steam and big companies like Epic Games proudly adopt the tech. A recent report even estimated that around 40 percent of active developers use AI tools in their work.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, smileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop. While the console's firmware has long since been updated to stop known jailbreak exploits, SmileBasic 4 itself has now also been patched.

SmileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing users to code their own simple programs and games. It's also opened multiple backdoors for jailbreak exploits over the years, first on 3DS, and then on Switch 2.

Technically, SmileBasic 4 is a Switch 1 game, but AI-backed hackers found a way to use it in order to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, allowing the machines to run code not approved by Nintendo. That would allow users to, in theory, run homebrew applications, but as far as I can tell, the exploit had not yet been extended to allow people to play pirated games.

Nonetheless, Nintendo acted quickly to delist SmileBasic 4 from the eShop and to patch the console's firmware to address the exploit at a system level. That's a necessary step, too, as SmileBasic 4 was not the only application that could be used to exploit it. Notably, Civilization 7, a game that is available on cartridge and thus impervious to delistings and software updates, could also be used for the jailbreak.

Sources indicate that even so, it seems that SmileBasic 4 itself has been updated to ensure that a similar exploit never happens again. As Twitter user MarioMasta64 notes, the software itself has gotten a latest update post-reinstatement aimed at closing the hole used for the jailbreak. The application's demo – which could also be used to exploit it – has also been updated, but it has not yet been relisted on the eShop.

Recent findings suggest that earlier this year in a bit of a shakeup for the fleshiest kid in town, Super Meat Boy entered into a new dimension in the aptly named Super Meat Boy 3D. I've not played it but it seems like a good take on the format. Clearly, though, sometimes you just need to play the hits, as a new release of the original game is on the way in the form of Super Meat Boy Again+, a remaster with updated graphics, levels and plenty more.

What is there is very clearly Super Meat Boy, uh, again, just with a big newly introduced lick of paint. There is probably some kind of joke to be made about it being DLSS yassified, but I'm too tired to think of one, so, you get the point. But it does look pretty good! I do kind of miss the Flash game aesthetic, I think there's a real charm to the sort of visual design sensibilities you'd find from that era, but this remaster certainly ain't ugly at least. Apparently it's not just the art that's new, as there's also new music, cutscenes, secrets and "stuff.".

If the animated sequences featured in the trailer, which you can have a gander at above, are included in the final game that'll be a treat to watch too, as I think they better capture the Newgrounds pseudo sub-genre of animation than the graphical overhaul. It sounds like they will be looking at the Steam page, so, a treat to look forward to while committing an act of masochism by playing it!

There's no release date attached to this remaster, so we'll all just have to sit tight for an update there. The original is still listed on Steam, but if you fancy as major a dose of nostalgia as the trailer is trying to present to you, you could always go play the original, plain old regular Meat Boy. It's playable right on Newgrounds thanks to the Flash emulator Ruffle and works like a dream! Or if you're happy to wait, you could always wishlist the new one on Steam.
